title: Halloween
cast: Jamie Lee Curtis, Donald Pleasence, Nancy Kyes
setting: Haddonfield, Illinois, a quiet suburb on Halloween night
plot: On Halloween night in 1963, six-year-old Michael Myers stabs his older sister to death and is locked away in a sanitarium. Fifteen years later, on October 30, he escapes and drives back to Haddonfield, with his psychiatrist Dr. Sam Loomis chasing him and warning anyone who will listen. Wearing a blank white mask, Michael silently stalks shy high school student Laurie Strode and her friends as they babysit around the neighborhood. One by one her friends stop answering the phone, and Laurie crosses the street to check on them while the kids she is watching stay behind.
ending: Laurie fights back with a knitting needle and a coat hanger, but Michael keeps getting up. Loomis arrives and shoots him six times, knocking him off the balcony. When Loomis looks down at the lawn, the body is gone.
note: The movie that set the rules for every slasher after it. Watch for the long opening shot through the mask.

title: The Thing
cast: Kurt Russell, Wilford Brimley, Keith David
setting: An isolated American research station in Antarctica
plot: A twelve-man research crew in Antarctica takes in a sled dog that was being chased across the ice by a Norwegian helicopter. That night the dog splits open in the kennel and reveals an alien organism that absorbs and perfectly imitates any living thing it touches. Helicopter pilot R.J. MacReady takes charge as paranoia spreads, because anyone in the room could already be the creature. He invents a blood test with a hot wire, ties the survivors to a couch, and waits to see whose blood jumps out of the dish.
ending: MacReady blows up the base with dynamite to freeze the creature out. He sits in the burning snow with Childs, the only other survivor, and neither man can be sure the other is human. They share a bottle and wait.
note: Practical effects that still hold up. Flopped in theaters, now a classic.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
cast: Heather Langenkamp, Johnny Depp, Robert Englund
setting: Elm Street in Springwood, Ohio
plot: Teenagers on Elm Street start having the same nightmare about a burned man in a striped sweater with knives for fingers. When Tina is killed in her sleep while her boyfriend watches, Nancy Thompson realizes that whatever kills you in the dream kills you for real. She learns that her parents and the other adults burned a child killer named Fred Krueger to death years ago, and now he is getting revenge through their children. Nancy drinks coffee, takes pills, and tries everything to stay awake while her boyfriend Glen keeps falling asleep.
ending: Nancy pulls Freddy into the real world and fills the house with booby traps. Then she turns her back on him, takes away his power, and he vanishes. In the final scene the car of friends locks itself and Nancy's mother is yanked through the front door window.
note: Johnny Depp's first movie role. Do not watch it right before bed.

title: Scream
cast: Neve Campbell, Courteney Cox, David Arquette, Skeet Ulrich, Matthew Lillard
setting: Woodsboro, a small town in California
plot: A year after her mother's murder, Sidney Prescott is still grieving when a masked killer in a Ghostface costume starts calling teenagers in Woodsboro and quizzing them about horror movies before killing them. Reporter Gale Weathers smells a story, Deputy Dewey tries to protect everyone, and video store clerk Randy explains the rules of surviving a horror movie: never have sex, never drink or do drugs, and never say you will be right back. Sidney suspects her boyfriend Billy, then doubts herself, as the killer closes in on a party at Stu's house.
ending: There are two killers: Billy Loomis and Stu Macher. Billy reveals he killed Sidney's mother because she broke up his family. Sidney turns their own tricks against them, kills Stu with a television and shoots Billy in the head.
note: A horror movie about horror movies. The opening scene with Drew Barrymore is legendary.

title: Friday the 13th
cast: Betsy Palmer, Adrienne King, Kevin Bacon
setting: Camp Crystal Lake, a summer camp in the New Jersey woods
plot: Camp Crystal Lake has been closed for more than twenty years after a boy drowned there and two counselors were murdered. Locals call it Camp Blood. A new group of young counselors arrives to fix the place up before reopening, ignoring a rambling warning from a man called Crazy Ralph. During a thunderstorm the power goes out, and someone the audience never fully sees picks off the counselors one at a time in the cabins, the archery range, and the showers, until only Alice is left.
ending: The killer is Pamela Voorhees, a friendly older woman who says she used to cook at the camp. Her son Jason drowned there in 1957 while counselors were not watching. Alice beheads her with a machete, then drifts out on the lake in a canoe, where a boy bursts out of the water and pulls her under.
note: Jason is not the killer in the first one. Kevin Bacon has a very bad night.

title: Sleepaway Camp
cast: Felissa Rose, Jonathan Tiersten, Mike Kellin
setting: Camp Arawak, a summer camp in upstate New York
plot: Painfully shy Angela Baker is sent to summer camp with her protective cousin Ricky years after a boating accident killed her father and brother. Angela barely speaks, refuses to swim, and gets bullied by other campers and a cruel counselor. Then the people who torment her start dying in increasingly strange accidents: a scalding pot of water in the kitchen, a drowning, a beehive dropped into a bathroom stall. The camp owner wants to keep it quiet so he does not lose business, and suspicion falls on hot-tempered Ricky.
ending: The final shot reveals that Angela is the killer, along with a notorious twist about who Angela really is, set up by a flashback to the boating accident. It is one of the most talked-about final images in horror.
note: Low budget, wildly dated, and the ending still makes people scream.

title: Fear Street Part Two: 1978
cast: Sadie Sink, Emily Rudd, Ted Sutherland, Gillian Jacobs
setting: Camp Nightwing, a summer camp in 1978
plot: Told as a flashback, the story follows sisters Ziggy and Cindy Berman during color war week at Camp Nightwing in the summer of 1978. Ziggy is a rebel who gets bullied, and Cindy is a rule-following counselor. When a counselor named Tommy is possessed by the curse of the witch Sarah Fier and starts killing campers with an axe, Cindy goes into the caves under the camp looking for the witch's grave, while Ziggy tries to survive the massacre above ground with the help of Nick Goode.
ending: Cindy dies, and Ziggy is briefly killed and revived. The adult survivor who has been calling herself C. Berman turns out to be Ziggy, not Cindy. The witch's hand was never buried with her bones, so the curse continues.
note: A Netflix trilogy that loves 70s and 80s slashers. Watch Part One first.

title: The Shining
cast: Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, Danny Lloyd
setting: The Overlook Hotel, snowed in for the winter in the Colorado Rockies
plot: Struggling writer Jack Torrance takes a job as the winter caretaker of the remote Overlook Hotel, bringing his wife Wendy and young son Danny. The hotel manager mentions that a previous caretaker murdered his family there. Danny has a psychic gift called the shining, which the hotel cook shares, and he sees twin girls in a hallway and something terrible in Room 237. As snow cuts them off, Jack stops writing, starts talking to a bartender who should not exist, and slowly turns against his family.
ending: Jack chases Danny into the frozen hedge maze with an axe. Danny backtracks over his own footprints, escapes with Wendy in a snowcat, and Jack freezes to death in the maze. The last shot shows Jack in a photo from a hotel ball in 1921.
note: Here's Johnny. Everyone has a theory about the final photograph.

title: The Exorcist
cast: Ellen Burstyn, Linda Blair, Max von Sydow, Jason Miller
setting: A townhouse in Georgetown, Washington, D.C.
plot: Actress Chris MacNeil is filming in Georgetown when her twelve-year-old daughter Regan starts acting strangely after playing with a Ouija board. Doctors run painful tests and find nothing. Regan's voice changes, her bed shakes, and the people around her start dying. Desperate, Chris turns to Father Damien Karras, a priest who is losing his faith after his mother's death. Karras becomes convinced Regan is possessed by a demon, and the church sends the elderly Father Lankester Merrin, who has faced this demon before.
ending: Merrin dies of a heart attack during the exorcism. Karras dares the demon to take him instead, and when it enters his body he throws himself out the window and dies on the steep stone steps outside. Regan recovers and remembers nothing.
note: People fainted in theaters in 1973. Still the benchmark for possession movies.

title: Hereditary
cast: Toni Collette, Alex Wolff, Milly Shapiro, Gabriel Byrne
setting: A remote family home in Utah
plot: After her secretive mother dies, miniature artist Annie Graham tries to hold her family together while her strange daughter Charlie draws dark pictures and makes clicking sounds with her tongue. A shocking accident on the way home from a party shatters the family, and teenage son Peter starts seeing things in the corners of rooms. A friendly woman from Annie's grief group teaches her a seance, and Annie discovers that her mother belonged to a cult that worships a demon king named Paimon.
ending: The cult has been planning everything. Annie is possessed and dies, and Peter's body is taken over by Paimon. In the treehouse, the naked cult members kneel and crown him as their king.
note: Toni Collette's performance is one of the best in the genre. The dinner scene.

title: Midsommar
cast: Florence Pugh, Jack Reynor, Will Poulter, William Jackson Harper
setting: Hårga, a sunlit commune in rural Sweden
plot: Reeling from a family tragedy, Dani tags along with her distant boyfriend Christian and his grad school friends on a trip to a midsummer festival in the Swedish commune where their friend Pelle grew up. The sun barely sets, the people dress in white, and everything is beautiful until the elders take part in a ritual that shocks the visitors. The friends start disappearing one by one, the commune keeps offering Dani a family that actually listens to her, and Christian keeps drifting further away.
ending: Dani wins a maypole dance and is crowned May Queen. She chooses Christian as the final sacrifice, and he is sewn into a bear carcass and burned in a temple with the others. As it burns, Dani slowly smiles.
note: A breakup movie dressed as a horror movie, shot almost entirely in daylight.

title: Get Out
cast: Daniel Kaluuya, Allison Williams, Catherine Keener, Bradley Whitford, LilRel Howery
setting: The Armitage family's lakeside estate in upstate New York
plot: Photographer Chris Washington goes with his white girlfriend Rose to meet her parents for the weekend. Her family is overly friendly, the Black housekeeper and groundskeeper act strangely, and at a garden party the older white guests ask Chris unsettling questions about his body. Rose's mother, a hypnotherapist, stirs her tea and sends Chris into the Sunken Place. His best friend Rod, a TSA agent back in the city, keeps calling with increasingly accurate theories about what is going on.
ending: The family transplants white people's brains into Black bodies. Rose was in on it. Chris escapes using cotton from the chair to block the hypnosis, and when police lights appear, it is Rod in a TSA car coming to get him.
note: Won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay. Funny and terrifying at once.

title: Us
cast: Lupita Nyong'o, Winston Duke, Elisabeth Moss, Shahadi Wright Joseph
setting: A summer beach house near Santa Cruz, California
plot: Adelaide Wilson has been haunted since childhood, when she wandered into a hall of mirrors on the Santa Cruz boardwalk and met a girl who looked exactly like her. Now on vacation with her husband and kids, she feels something is wrong. That night four figures in red jumpsuits holding golden scissors stand in their driveway, and they are exact copies of the family. The doubles, called the Tethered, are rising up across the country, and they want to trade places with the people above.
ending: Adelaide kills her double, Red, in the tunnels under the boardwalk. Then she remembers the truth: as a child she was the Tethered girl, and she dragged the real Adelaide underground and took her place.
note: Lupita Nyong'o plays two completely different people. Listen for the remix of I Got 5 on It.

title: Nope
cast: Daniel Kaluuya, Keke Palmer, Steven Yeun
setting: A horse ranch in Agua Dulce, California
plot: After their father is killed by debris falling from the sky, siblings OJ and Emerald Haywood try to keep the family business of training horses for Hollywood alive. They notice a cloud that never moves over their ranch, and horses keep vanishing. Convinced it is a flying saucer, they decide to get the perfect photo of it and get rich, teaming up with an electronics store employee and a famous cinematographer. Their neighbor, a former child star who runs a western theme park, has been feeding horses to the thing in the sky.
ending: The UFO is actually a living creature they name Jean Jacket, and it eats anyone who looks at it. OJ distracts it on horseback while Emerald gets the shot with an old hand-crank well camera, and the creature dies swallowing a giant inflatable balloon.
note: A monster movie about spectacle and the people who get eaten by it.

title: The Conjuring
cast: Vera Farmiga, Patrick Wilson, Lili Taylor, Ron Livingston
setting: The Perron family farmhouse in Harrisville, Rhode Island, in 1971
plot: Carolyn and Roger Perron move into an old farmhouse with their five daughters. The dog refuses to come inside, every clock stops at 3:07 in the morning, and the girls are pulled by their feet in bed. Paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren, who keep a room full of cursed objects including a doll named Annabelle, agree to help. Lorraine discovers that the land once belonged to Bathsheba, a woman who sacrificed her baby to the devil and cursed anyone who took her land.
ending: Bathsheba possesses Carolyn, who tries to kill one of her daughters. Ed performs the exorcism himself, and Lorraine reminds Carolyn of a happy memory with her family, which gives her the strength to push the spirit out.
note: Based on a case the real Warrens investigated. Kicked off a whole cinematic universe.

title: Insidious
cast: Patrick Wilson, Rose Byrne, Lin Shaye, Ty Simpkins
setting: A suburban family home, and a dark spirit world called The Further
plot: Shortly after Josh and Renai Lambert move into a new house, their son Dalton falls off a ladder in the attic and slips into a coma that doctors cannot explain. Strange voices come through the baby monitor and figures appear in the windows, so the family moves, but the hauntings follow them. Psychic Elise Rainier explains that the house is not haunted: Dalton is. He can leave his body while he sleeps, and he has wandered so far into The Further that spirits are lining up to take his empty body.
ending: Josh enters The Further and brings Dalton back. But when Elise photographs Josh afterwards, she sees the old woman who has haunted him since childhood. He strangles Elise, and he is no longer Josh.
note: The red-faced demon scene behind Josh is the jump scare people still talk about.

title: Saw
cast: Cary Elwes, Leigh Whannell, Tobin Bell, Danny Glover
setting: A filthy industrial bathroom
plot: Photographer Adam and surgeon Dr. Lawrence Gordon wake up chained to pipes at opposite ends of a run-down bathroom, with a dead body lying between them holding a gun and a tape recorder. Each finds a cassette from a killer called Jigsaw, who puts people he thinks waste their lives into deadly traps. Gordon is told he must kill Adam by six o'clock or his wife and daughter will die. Flashbacks show a detective hunting Jigsaw and earlier victims of his games, while the two men find hacksaws that are too weak to cut the chains.
ending: Gordon saws off his own foot and crawls away to get help. Then the dead body in the middle of the room stands up. It is Jigsaw, John Kramer, who watched the whole time, and he says game over and slams the door, leaving Adam in the dark.
note: Made for about a million dollars. Spawned ten sequels.

title: Oculus
cast: Karen Gillan, Brenton Thwaites, Katee Sackhoff, Rory Cochrane
setting: The family home of Kaylie and Tim Russell, with an antique mirror
plot: Eleven years ago, Tim Russell shot his father after his father tortured and killed their mother. Tim was locked in a psychiatric hospital, but his sister Kaylie always blamed the Lasser Glass, an antique mirror that has been linked to dozens of deaths over centuries. Now that Tim is released, Kaylie tracks down the mirror, sets it up in their childhood home, and surrounds it with cameras, plants, a dog, and a kill switch with a swinging anchor, to prove the mirror is evil. The mirror starts making them see things that are not there.
ending: The mirror tricks Tim into triggering the anchor trap while Kaylie stands in front of it, killing her. Police arrive and arrest Tim, who screams that it was the mirror, just like when he was a child.
note: The present day and the past blur together in the same rooms. Mike Flanagan's breakout.

title: Hush
cast: Kate Siegel, John Gallagher Jr., Michael Trucco
setting: An isolated house in the woods
plot: Maddie Young is a writer who lost her hearing and her voice after meningitis as a teenager. She lives alone in a house in the woods, finishing her second novel. One night a masked man with a crossbow kills her neighbor outside her glass door, and Maddie never hears a thing. When he realizes she is deaf, he decides to toy with her instead of breaking in right away, cutting her power and internet and taking her phone. Maddie has to outthink a killer she cannot hear coming, using her writer's habit of imagining every possible ending.
ending: Maddie sets off her smoke alarm to disorient him, then stabs him in the neck with a corkscrew. She survives as the police arrive, and her cat comes back too.
note: Co-written by Kate Siegel and Mike Flanagan. Almost no dialogue.

title: Gerald's Game
cast: Carla Gugino, Bruce Greenwood, Carel Struycken
setting: A remote lake house in Alabama
plot: Jessie and Gerald drive to their isolated lake house to save their marriage. Gerald handcuffs Jessie to the bed as part of a game, then suffers a heart attack and dies, leaving her chained with no one coming. A stray dog wanders in through the open door and starts eating Gerald's body. Dehydrated and alone, Jessie argues with visions of Gerald and of herself, confronts a buried memory from a solar eclipse when she was a child, and sees a tall, pale figure carrying a box of bones standing in the corner at night.
ending: Jessie slices her wrist on a broken glass and pulls her hand out of the cuff, tearing the skin off. She escapes, and later learns the Moonlight Man was real: a serial killer named Joubert. She faces him in court and tells him he is so much smaller than she remembered.
note: Based on a Stephen King book people called unfilmable.

title: Doctor Sleep
cast: Ewan McGregor, Rebecca Ferguson, Kyliegh Curran
setting: A small New Hampshire town, and the abandoned Overlook Hotel
plot: Decades after surviving the Overlook Hotel, Danny Torrance is a recovering alcoholic working at a hospice, where he uses his shining to comfort dying patients. He connects telepathically with Abra Stone, a girl with an even more powerful gift. Abra senses a group called the True Knot, led by Rose the Hat, who travel the country in RVs and torture children with the shining to eat the steam they release, which keeps them young. When the True Knot comes after Abra, Danny has to protect her.
ending: Danny lures Rose to the snowed-in Overlook and wakes the hotel's ghosts, who devour her. Possessed by the hotel, Danny fights it off and lets the boiler explode, dying in the fire. He later appears to Abra as a ghost.
note: A sequel to The Shining that tries to please both Stephen King and Kubrick fans.

title: X
cast: Mia Goth, Jenna Ortega, Brittany Snow, Martin Henderson, Kid Cudi
setting: A rural farm in Texas in 1979
plot: In 1979 a small film crew rents a guest house on a remote Texas farm to secretly shoot an adult movie, hoping to cash in on the home video boom. Aspiring star Maxine is sure she is meant to be famous. The elderly farmer Howard does not know what they are filming, and his wife Pearl watches the young visitors from the windows with longing and jealousy over the youth she lost. That night, after the crew argues about the movie, Pearl and Howard start killing them one by one, near a lake with an alligator in it.
ending: Maxine survives. Pearl dies after Maxine runs her over with a truck, and Howard dies of a heart attack. A TV in the house shows a preacher, revealing that Maxine is his runaway daughter.
note: Mia Goth plays both Maxine and the elderly Pearl. Watch Pearl next.

title: Pearl
cast: Mia Goth, David Corenswet, Tandi Wright
setting: A Texas farm in 1918
plot: In 1918, during the flu pandemic, young Pearl lives on her family's farm with her strict German mother and her sick father while her husband Howard is away fighting in the war. Pearl dreams of escaping to become a dancer in the movies, and she sneaks into town to watch films and meets a charming projectionist. When she hears about a dance audition at the church, she becomes obsessed with winning, and anyone who stands between her and stardom, including her own family and an alligator in the pond, starts paying for it.
ending: Pearl loses the audition and kills the girl who wins it. When Howard comes home from the war, Pearl greets him at the door with a huge, forced smile that she holds through the entire end credits.
note: A prequel to X shot in bright Technicolor, like a Disney movie gone wrong.

title: The Babadook
cast: Essie Davis, Noah Wiseman, Daniel Henshall
setting: A gray house in Adelaide, Australia
plot: Amelia is a widowed mother whose husband died in a car crash while driving her to the hospital to give birth. Six years later she is exhausted, and her son Samuel is anxious and difficult, building weapons to fight imaginary monsters. One night Samuel pulls a red pop-up book called Mister Babadook from the shelf. It describes a figure in a top hat who will not leave once you let him in. Amelia tears up the book, but it reappears on her doorstep, taped back together with new pages showing her hurting her son.
ending: Amelia stands up to the Babadook and drives it into the basement. She does not destroy it. Instead she keeps it locked downstairs and feeds it a bowl of worms, a picture of living with grief instead of defeating it.
note: A debut feature from Jennifer Kent. The monster is grief.

title: The Witch
cast: Anya Taylor-Joy, Ralph Ineson, Kate Dickie, Harvey Scrimshaw
setting: An isolated farm at the edge of a forest in 1630s New England
plot: In the 1630s, a Puritan family is banished from their colony and builds a farm next to a dark forest. While teenage Thomasin is playing peekaboo with her baby brother Samuel, he vanishes. The crops fail, the goat named Black Phillip seems to talk to the youngest twins, and the family begins accusing Thomasin of witchcraft. When her brother Caleb comes back from the woods sick and raving, the family's faith and paranoia tear them apart.
ending: Thomasin's whole family dies. Alone, she asks Black Phillip to speak, and he asks her if she would like to live deliciously. She signs his book, walks into the woods, and rises into the air with a coven of witches around a fire.
note: The dialogue comes from real 17th-century diaries. Anya Taylor-Joy's first lead role.

title: It Follows
cast: Maika Monroe, Keir Gilchrist, Daniel Zovatto
setting: The suburbs of Detroit, Michigan
plot: After sleeping with her new boyfriend, nineteen-year-old Jay wakes up tied to a wheelchair. He explains that he has passed a curse to her: an entity will follow her, walking slowly, looking like a stranger or someone she loves, and if it catches her it will kill her and then come back for him. The only escape is to sleep with someone else and pass it on. Jay and her friends drive around Detroit trying to outrun something that never stops walking toward her.
ending: The friends try to trap the entity in a swimming pool and electrocute it, and it fails. Jay sleeps with her friend Paul. The final shot shows them walking hand in hand down a street, with a figure walking slowly behind them.
note: Great synth score. You will watch the background of every shot.

title: The Ring
cast: Naomi Watts, Martin Henderson, Daveigh Chase, Brian Cox
setting: Seattle and an island off the coast of Washington State
plot: Seattle reporter Rachel Keller investigates the death of her niece, one of four teenagers who died on the same night, exactly one week after watching a strange videotape at a cabin. Rachel finds the tape and watches it: a ring of light, a chair, a ladder, a well. The phone rings, and a voice whispers seven days. Racing her own deadline, Rachel and her ex Noah trace the images to Anna Morgan, a horse breeder on Moesko Island, and her adopted daughter Samara, a girl who could burn images into film.
ending: Rachel finds Samara's body at the bottom of the well and gives her a proper burial, thinking she broke the curse. But Noah dies anyway. Rachel realizes she survived only because she made a copy of the tape and showed it to someone else.
note: A remake of the Japanese film Ringu. Samara climbing out of the TV.

title: The Blair Witch Project
cast: Heather Donahue, Michael C. Williams, Joshua Leonard
setting: The Black Hills Forest near Burkittsville, Maryland
plot: In 1994, three film students hike into the woods near Burkittsville, Maryland, to make a documentary about the legend of the Blair Witch. The footage, presented as recovered after they disappeared, shows them getting lost. They wake to strange noises around their tent, find piles of rocks outside it, and see stick figures hanging from the trees. Their map vanishes, they walk in circles for days, and one morning Josh is gone. That night they hear him screaming in the dark.
ending: Heather and Mike find an abandoned house. Mike runs into the basement and goes silent. Heather follows with the camera and finds him standing still, facing the corner. Then she is hit, and the camera falls to the floor.
note: The marketing convinced people it was real. Started the found footage boom.

title: Paranormal Activity
cast: Katie Featherston, Micah Sloat
setting: A two-story tract house in San Diego
plot: Katie has been followed by a presence since childhood, and now it has followed her to the house she shares with her boyfriend Micah. Micah buys a camera and sets it up on a tripod in their bedroom to record what happens while they sleep. Doors move, footsteps appear in baby powder on the floor, and a psychic tells them it is a demon, not a ghost, and that they should not talk to it. Micah ignores him and buys a Ouija board.
ending: Katie stands by the bed for hours, walks downstairs, and screams for Micah. He runs to her. Footsteps come back up the stairs, Micah's body is thrown at the camera, and Katie crouches over him, smiles, and lunges at the lens.
note: Shot in the director's own house for about fifteen thousand dollars.

title: The Cabin in the Woods
cast: Kristen Connolly, Chris Hemsworth, Fran Kranz, Richard Jenkins, Bradley Whitford
setting: A cabin in the woods, and a secret underground control facility
plot: Five college friends drive to a remote cabin for the weekend. In the basement they find old objects, and Dana reads aloud from a diary, which summons a family of zombie hillbillies. Meanwhile, two technicians in an underground facility are watching every move on monitors, releasing chemicals to make the kids act like horror movie stereotypes, and taking bets on which monster they will pick. Stoner Marty starts to suspect that someone is controlling them.
ending: The facility exists to sacrifice young people to ancient gods each year. Dana and Marty reach the facility, release every monster at once, and refuse to finish the ritual. A giant hand rises from the earth and the world ends.
note: Every horror monster you can name shows up in the elevator scene.

title: Evil Dead II
cast: Bruce Campbell, Sarah Berry, Dan Hicks
setting: A cabin in the Tennessee woods
plot: Ash takes his girlfriend Linda to a remote cabin and plays a tape of a professor reading from the Necronomicon, the Book of the Dead. An evil force possesses Linda, and Ash has to kill her. Trapped in the cabin, he fights off the force as his own hand becomes possessed and attacks him, so he cuts it off with a chainsaw. The professor's daughter arrives with missing pages from the book, and together with some locals they try to send the evil back.
ending: Ash opens a portal that sucks the evil away, and him with it. He lands in the year 1300 with a chainsaw on his arm, where knights see him kill a flying demon and hail him as a hero.
note: Groovy. Half remake, half sequel, all Bruce Campbell.

title: Alien
cast: Sigourney Weaver, Tom Skerritt, John Hurt, Ian Holm
setting: The commercial towing spaceship Nostromo, in deep space
plot: The crew of the space freighter Nostromo is woken from hypersleep to answer a distress signal from a moon. On the surface, Kane finds a chamber full of eggs, and a creature leaps out and attaches itself to his face. Back on the ship it falls off and Kane seems fine, until dinner, when an alien bursts out of his chest and escapes into the ship's vents. As the creature grows and hunts the crew, warrant officer Ripley discovers the company wanted the alien brought back all along.
ending: Ripley sets the ship to self-destruct and escapes in the shuttle with Jones the cat, only to find the alien hiding on board. She suits up, opens the airlock, and blasts it into space with a grappling gun.
note: In space, no one can hear you scream. Ripley is the original final girl in space.

title: Talk to Me
cast: Sophie Wilde, Alexandra Jensen, Joe Bird, Miranda Otto
setting: Suburban homes in Adelaide, Australia
plot: Mia, a teenager still grieving her mother, goes with her best friend Jade to a party where kids pass around an embalmed hand covered in graffiti. If you light a candle, hold the hand, and say talk to me, you see a spirit. Say I let you in, and it possesses you, which the kids film for their phones. The rule is ninety seconds, never longer. When Jade's little brother Riley holds on too long and the spirit claiming to be Mia's mother takes over, everything goes wrong.
ending: Mia believes the spirits want her to kill Riley so her mother can be freed. She stops herself, steps in front of a car, and dies. She wakes up as a spirit in the dark on the other side of the hand, now the one being summoned.
note: Made by YouTubers RackaRacka. Do not hold the hand for more than ninety seconds.

title: Smile
cast: Sosie Bacon, Jessie T. Usher, Kyle Gallner
setting: A psychiatric hospital and suburbs in New Jersey
plot: Dr. Rose Cotter, an overworked psychiatrist, meets a terrified graduate student who says an entity wearing a creepy smile has been following her. The student then smiles at Rose and kills herself in front of her. Rose starts seeing smiling people everywhere, ruins her nephew's birthday party, and her fiance and therapist think she is having a breakdown. With help from her ex, a detective, she discovers a chain of suicides, each witnessed by the next victim, going back years.
ending: Rose confronts the entity in her childhood home, where her mother died, and thinks she has won. But she is still in its grip, and she sets herself on fire in front of her ex Joel, passing the curse to him.
note: The marketing put smiling actors in the crowd at baseball games.

title: Barbarian
cast: Georgina Campbell, Bill Skarsgård, Justin Long
setting: A double-booked rental house in Detroit's Brightmoor neighborhood
plot: Tess arrives late at night at her rental house in Detroit for a job interview, and finds that a man named Keith has already booked it. It is raining and every hotel is full, so she warily agrees to stay. The next day she goes looking for toilet paper in the basement and finds a hidden door, a narrow hallway, and a room with a bed, a bucket, and a camcorder. Then the movie suddenly cuts to a sitcom actor named AJ in California who owns the house and needs to sell it.
ending: Under the house lives the Mother, created by a man who kidnapped women decades ago. She keeps Tess and AJ as her babies. On a water tower, AJ pushes Tess off to save himself, and the Mother catches her and falls with AJ. Tess shoots the Mother as she cradles her.
note: Go in knowing nothing. The less you know, the better.

title: Train to Busan
cast: Gong Yoo, Ma Dong-seok, Jung Yu-mi, Kim Su-an
setting: A KTX high-speed train from Seoul to Busan, South Korea
plot: Workaholic fund manager Seok-woo takes his young daughter Su-an on a train from Seoul to Busan to see her mother for her birthday. Just before the doors close, an infected woman stumbles aboard, and a zombie outbreak spreads through the cars at full speed while the country collapses outside the windows. Seok-woo teams up with tough working-class husband Sang-hwa and his pregnant wife Seong-kyeong, while a selfish executive puts everyone at risk to save himself.
ending: Seok-woo is bitten and walks off the back of the moving train to protect his daughter. Su-an and Seong-kyeong walk through a dark tunnel toward Busan, and soldiers almost shoot them until they hear Su-an singing the song she practiced for her father.
note: Fast zombies in a confined space. You will cry.

title: 28 Days Later
cast: Cillian Murphy, Naomie Harris, Brendan Gleeson, Christopher Eccleston
setting: An empty London and the English countryside
plot: Animal rights activists break into a lab and release chimpanzees infected with Rage, a virus that turns people into violent, sprinting killers within seconds. Twenty-eight days later, bike courier Jim wakes up from a coma in an empty hospital and walks across a deserted Westminster Bridge. He joins survivors Selena, Frank, and Frank's daughter Hannah, and they follow a radio broadcast to a military blockade near Manchester that promises safety and a cure.
ending: The soldiers plan to force Selena and Hannah into becoming their wives. Jim fights his way back and rescues them. Weeks later, the three of them spread a giant fabric sign spelling HELLO in a field as a jet flies overhead.
note: Shot on early digital video. The empty London scenes were filmed at dawn.

title: Candyman
cast: Virginia Madsen, Tony Todd, Xander Berkeley
setting: The Cabrini-Green housing projects in Chicago
plot: Graduate student Helen Lyle is writing a thesis on urban legends when she hears about Candyman, a ghost with a hook for a hand who appears if you say his name five times in a mirror. The legend leads her to the Cabrini-Green housing projects, where residents connect him to real murders. Helen dismisses the legend, says his name in the mirror, and soon a tall man in a long coat appears, wanting her to become part of his story. People around her start dying, and the police believe Helen is the killer.
ending: Candyman kidnaps a baby and lures Helen into a giant bonfire. She saves the baby but dies in the flames. When her unfaithful husband says her name in the mirror, Helen appears with the hook and kills him, becoming a legend herself.
note: Tony Todd's voice. Do not say his name five times.
